title: Steam Generator
model_title: Packaged Steam Generator (3-Pass Dry-Back Fire-Tube Boiler)

introduction.definition: A packaged steam generator (fire-tube or shell boiler) makes steam for heating and process use. The burner fires into a large furnace tube; the hot gases turn in a reversal chamber and pass back and forth through banks of smoke tubes (2nd and 3rd passes) before leaving through the stack. All these heating surfaces are surrounded by water inside the shell.
applications: Factories, hospitals, food and textile plants
Up to roughly 20–30 t/h steam at moderate pressure
key_points: Hot gas inside tubes, water outside (fire-tube)
Large water content → stable under load swings
introduction.summary: A packaged steam generator (shell or fire-tube boiler) produces steam for heating and process use. Hot combustion gases from the burner pass through the furnace tube and then through two banks of smoke tubes (three passes), all surrounded by water inside the pressure shell. Steam collects above the water level and leaves via the main steam valve.

foundation: Level concrete plinth/foundation designed for operating weight full of water; allow access for tube cleaning and burner maintenance.
alignment: Level the boiler; align burner and fan; check expansion allowances on headers and casings.
piping: Fit safety valves with unobstructed discharge piped to a safe place; feedwater with check and isolation valves; blowdown to a blowdown vessel.
Flue/stack sized for the draught required; explosion relief where specified.
commissioning: Boil-out/chemical clean; hydro-test; set and test safety valves; test low-water cut-outs and flame safeguard (purge, ignition, flame failure); tune combustion (O₂, CO).

routine.task: Check water level gauges, blowdown, low-water alarm test.

overhaul.task: Statutory inspection; internal/external examination; safety valve overhaul.

lubrication: Burner fan motor bearings greased; no lubrication for pressure parts.

causes: Failed level control, feed pump trip
remedies: Test cut-outs; never add cold water to an overheated boiler

safety: Operate only with tested safety valves, level controls and flame safeguard; blowdown safely.

video_tutorials.title: Steam Generator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Steam Generator.
A packaged steam generator (fire-tube or shell boiler) makes steam for heating and process use.
The burner fires into a large furnace tube; the hot gases turn in a reversal chamber and pass back and forth through banks of smoke tubes (2nd and 3rd passes) before leaving through the stack.
All these heating surfaces are surrounded by water inside the shell.
Typical applications include factories, hospitals, food and textile plants; district and process heating; up to roughly 20–30 t/h steam at moderate pressure.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Pressure Shell & End Plates (water/steam side), Rear Reversal Chamber (refractory-lined door: turns gas from furnace into 2nd pass), Front Smoke Box (2nd→3rd pass turn), Rear Smoke Box & Stack.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Steam Generator works.
The burner mixes fuel and air and fires into the furnace tube (1st pass).
The flame radiates heat to the furnace wall and water around it.
Gases turn in the rear reversal chamber into the 2nd-pass tubes.
The front smoke box turns them into the 3rd pass and on to the stack.
Water boils around the tubes; steam leaves through the main steam valve.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Steam Generator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Steam Generator.
Check water level gauges, blowdown, low-water alarm test.
Combustion check (O₂/CO), clean tubes.
Statutory inspection; internal/external examination; safety valve overhaul.
Watch for low water / overheating: furnace deformation, cracks. Common cause: failed level control, feed pump trip.
Watch for scale formation: rising stack temperature, overheating. Common cause: poor water treatment.
Watch for flame failure: lockout. Common cause: fuel supply, ignition, flame sensor.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
